body_text:
Last Call

Nina inherits The Last Call, her late uncle's failing dive bar — and the debt he owed to the man who really owns the block. The bartender came with the building and knows where every body is buried. A regular with money keeps tipping like he's buying something. The cook runs the kitchen like it's hers. The supplier sets his own terms. And every week, the collector knocks. Keep the lights on, or lose the only thing she's got left.

We're a small indie studio crafting intimate, story-driven experiences. Every game is made with care, and your support helps us keep creating. If you enjoy our work, consider supporting us!

body_text:
Canvas: First night (canvas_first_night) | Node: First night



The keys still have his keyring on them — a bottle opener worn smooth and a faded tag that says NOT THE GOOD WHISKEY in his handwriting. The lock sticks the way he always said it did. Inside, the dark smells exactly like it did when you were nineteen and he let you sit at the end of the bar with a Coke and watch him work.

You find the lights behind the register. The Last Call comes up around you one buzzing fixture at a time — the cracked booths, the dead letter in the beer sign, the jukebox squatting in the corner like it's waiting to be asked.

A man is wiping down the taps like he never stopped. Big, grey, a towel on his shoulder. He doesn't startle when the lights come on. He just looks at you the way you'd look at weather you'd been expecting.

You'd be Sully's niece. He talked about you. I'm Sal — I pour, I lock up, I been doing both since before you could see over the bar.

Ask about the envelope by the register.

Canvas: The Last Call — a message from Boyd (canvas_shark_summons) | Node: He wants to see you



The Collector takes the cash like always, but this time he doesn't leave after. He sets a card on the bar — an address three blocks off Main, no name on it — and taps it once with a finger like a man closing a deal you didn't agree to.

Mr. Boyd likes to meet the people who owe him, now you're the one who does. That's a courtesy, by the way — he doesn't usually. Tomorrow. Bring yourself, not excuses.

body_text:
Canvas: The Last Call — Sal (canvas_sal_ropes_first) | Node: Working the bar



Sal doesn't ask if you know what you're doing. He just slides down the bar to make room and starts talking — which tap pours foam until you crack the line, which regular runs a tab and which one you cut off at three, where Sully kept the good stuff and why nobody's allowed to touch it.

You keep up. You've poured in worse rooms than this. Somewhere around the second rush he stops narrating and just works beside you, and that's its own kind of test passed — the quiet one, where he decides you're not going to embarrass the place.

Huh. You've done this. Sully said you tended in the city. I figured he was bragging.

💭 You are thinking: First thing today that felt like solid ground.







Let him show you how Sully ran the place.
